summary.text: 休 is commonly interpreted as a person beside a tree, with the scene suggesting rest. A competing interpretation identifies the right-hand element as military marker posts and connects the graph with commendation; the original motivation remains disputed.

formation.text: The common analysis treats 休 as a semantic compound: 人 depicts a person and 木 a tree, together suggesting rest in the tree’s shade. Some early forms are interpreted as showing the tree top bending toward the person. A competing analysis reads the right-hand element as 禾-like marker posts associated with recognition of military merit.

components.text: In the common analysis, 人 depicts the person in the resting scene. The competing account disputes the interpretation of the whole graph but offers no alternative account of this element.

In the common analysis, 木 depicts the tree; some early forms are interpreted as bending its top toward the person to suggest shade. This reading distinguishes it from 禾 despite a resemblance in some forms. The competing marker-post interpretation disputes the identification.

history.text: Catalogs list 休 among oracle-bone and bronze examples and in the seal-script category, but the cited records do not give a sequence of graphic changes.

The transmitted Shuowen account defines 休 as “cease; rest” and explains it as a person relying on a tree. A competing account instead proposes 禾-like paired markers at a military gate. These interpretations disagree about the graph’s original motivation.

uncertainties.text: The person-and-tree interpretation and the military marker-post interpretation disagree about the right-hand element and original motivation; the available accounts do not resolve the dispute.
The cited bronze and received-text uses have no securely established order here, so the earliest lexical sense cannot be ranked confidently.

senses.text: Rest is supported by received-text examples and the transmitted Shuowen definition, but the earliest attested sense cannot be ranked securely.
休 is used to mean “stop” or “cease.” The cited examples do not establish when this use arose relative to “rest.”
One proposed connection links resting in shade with shelter or protection. The cited uses do not establish the chronology or each step in that development.
Reported inscriptional uses include favor or reward. Their relationship to rest or shelter is uncertain.
A competing graph analysis cites a bronze use glossed “good” or “commendable” and connects it with recognition of merit. This use does not settle the graph’s origin or the sense’s chronology.
The common current meaning includes resting or taking a break.

developments.text: Both meanings are attested, but the available evidence does not show that one developed from the other.

limitations.text: The earliest lexical sense cannot be ranked securely. Proposed connections among shade, protection, favor, reward, goodness, pleasure, rest, and stopping do not establish a proven sequence.

overview.text: 休 is commonly explained as a person resting beside a tree: 人 and 木 form the scene. Another interpretation reads the right side as military marker posts, so the graph’s original motivation remains uncertain.

components.text: 人 depicts the person in the common person-and-tree scene.
木 depicts the tree in the common analysis; the marker-post interpretation disputes this identification.

relationships.text: In the common person-and-tree interpretation, 人 depicts the person in the scene represented by 休.
In the common analysis, 木 depicts the tree beside which the person rests; the marker-post interpretation disputes this identification.
